example_usages: Lalique museum [Museum] --maximumAttendeeCapacity--> 650 [Quantity] || Washington state wildfires cause evacuations of 60,000 people [WildfireEvacuation] --maximumAttendeeCapacity--> 60,000 people [StatisticalPopulation]
model_justification: Schema.org's maximumAttendeeCapacity (Place→Integer) fits Museum→Quantity as a capacity measure. | The evacuation event's evacuee count aligns with the attendee capacity schema.org property, as both relate to a numeric population affected.

schema_definition: The number of employees in an organization, e.g. business.
example_usages: Microsoft Job Cuts and Xbox Restructuring [JobCutsAndRestructuring] --numberOfEmployees--> 4,800 jobs [Number] || Microsoft [Organization] --numberOfEmployees--> 9,000 jobs [Number]
model_justification: numberOfEmployees fits Organization → Number and JobCutsAndRestructuring → Number

schema_definition:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:

* Use the [[priceCurrency]] property (with standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS)
example_usages: Australian Open 2025 [SportsEvent] --price--> £47m [MonetaryAmount] || US Open [SportsEvent] --price--> £67.3m ($90m) [MonetaryAmount]
model_justification: Schema.org 'price' aligns with SportsEvent to MonetaryAmount for prize money values in event context.

schema_definition: The number or other unique designator assigned to a Report by the publishing organization.
example_usages: Ebola case in Haut-Uele province [Event] --reportNumber--> AFP [Organization] || Ebola case in Tshopo province [Event] --reportNumber--> Reuters [Organization]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Ebola case --reportNumber--> AFP"; reportNumber takes a designator string.

schema_definition: A modifiable or non-modifiable factor that increases the risk of a patient contracting this condition, e.g. age, coexisting condition.
example_usages: AI tool could spread misinformation [MisinformationRisk] --riskFactor--> Henk van Ess [Person] || AI erodes trust in satellite imagery [TrustErosion] --riskFactor--> Bill Greer [Person]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: riskFactor is scoped to MedicalCondition.

schema_definition: A pointer from a newer variant of a product to its previous, often discontinued predecessor.
example_usages: Activision-Blizzard [Organization] --successorOf--> Xbox 2024 Staff Reductions [JobCutsAndRestructuring] || Google retracts AI tool [ProductRetraction] --successorOf--> Nano Banana 2 [SoftwareApplication]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate | successorOf inverse fits JobCutsAndRestructuring → Organization
judge_notes: "Google --successorOf--> Earth AI tool".

schema_definition: The "temporal" property can be used in cases where more specific properties (e.g. [[temporalCoverage]], [[dateCreated]], [[dateModified]], [[datePublished]]) are not known to be appropriate.
example_usages: Jewelry theft at Lalique museum [Event] --temporal--> Sunday [Date] || Jewelry theft at Lalique museum [Event] --temporal--> 5:30 am [Time]
model_justification: Schema.org's temporal property accommodates Event→Date/Time as a general temporal relation.

schema_definition: A geographical region, typically under the jurisdiction of a particular government.
example_usages: "Kharkiv region" (Entity) as AdministrativeArea || "Chocó province" (Entity) as AdministrativeArea
model_justification: Bashkortostan, Yaroslavl, Kharkiv region, and Dnipropetrovsk region are all administrative divisions within countries. | Mentions like 'Chocó province' fit schema.org AdministrativeArea as a governed geographical region.

schema_definition: An intangible type to be applied to any archive content, carrying with it a set of properties required to describe archival items and collections.
example_usages: "Copiale cipher" (Entity) as ArchiveComponent || "105-page manuscript" (Entity) as ArchiveComponent
model_justification: Historical ciphers are archival items with encoded content, fitting schema.org's ArchiveComponent.

schema_definition: A chemical substance is 'a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types' (source: [ChEBI:59999](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=59999)).
example_usages: "artificial colorings" (Entity) as ChemicalSubstance || "saturated fats" (Entity) as ChemicalSubstance
model_justification: Schema.org ChemicalSubstance matches examples like 'sodium' and 'emulsifiers' as specific substances.

schema_definition: One of the continents (for example, Europe or Africa).
example_usages: "Europe" (Entity) as Continent
model_justification: Schema.org's Continent class matches the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention 'Europe'.

schema_definition: A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see Chapter 5.4 of ISO 8601).
example_usages: "17:30 ET" (Entity) as DateTime || "2026-08-05T20:00:00" (Entity) as DateTime
model_justification: 2026-08-05T20:00:00 is a specific point in time with both date and time components as defined by schema.org's DateTime. | Examples include specific time points with time zones.

schema_definition: A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Regio
example_usages: "42,000 hectares" (Entity) as DefinedRegion || "Var region" (Entity) as DefinedRegion
model_justification: The mention '42,000 hectares' refers to a measurable geographic region, aligning with the schema.org DefinedRegion class for non-political regions. | The mentions 'Gironde region' and 'Var region' refer to non-sovereign administrative regions within a country, fitting the schema.org DefinedRegion class.
judge_notes: "42,000 hectares" is an area measurement, not a defined region.

schema_definition: Properties that take Distances as values are of the form '<Number> <Length unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 ft'.
example_usages: "1,300km" (Entity) as Distance || "37 miles" (Entity) as Distance
model_justification: 1,300km and 700km are numerical values with units of length fitting schema.org's Distance class. | Distance matches the numerical value with unit in '37 miles', representing a measurable length.

schema_definition: An enterprise (potentially individual but typically collaborative), planned to achieve a particular aim. Use properties from [[Organization]], [[subOrganization]]/[[parentOrganization]] to indicate project sub-structures.
example_usages: "Descrypt project" (Entity) as Project
model_justification: The mention 'Descrypt project' fits schema.org's Project class as a collaborative initiative.

schema_definition: A PublicationEvent corresponds indifferently to the event of publication for a CreativeWork of any type, e.g. a broadcast event, an on-demand event, a book/journal publication via a variety of delivery media.
example_usages: "Production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day" (Event) as PublicationEvent
model_justification: Schema.org PublicationEvent aligns with the example of movie production as a release event.
judge_notes: Film production is typed as a publication event.

schema_definition: A screening of a movie or other video.
example_usages: "Minions & Monsters domestic performance" (Event) as ScreeningEvent || "Toy Story 5 domestic performance" (Event) as ScreeningEvent
model_justification: Schema.org ScreeningEvent aligns with the examples of movie showings and box office performance.
judge_notes: A box-office performance figure is typed as a screening.

schema_definition: A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[Statisti
example_usages: "60,000 people" (Entity) as StatisticalPopulation || "1,500 inhabitants" (Entity) as StatisticalPopulation
model_justification: Mentions are numerical counts of people, aligning with statistical population definitions. | StatisticalPopulation represents a set of instances (e.g., people) for analysis, fitting the numerical mention '1,500 inhabitants' as a population group.
judge_notes: "60,000 people" is a count, not a constrained set definition.

schema_definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].
example_usages: "Trump-Zelensky phone call on 2026-07-05" (Event) as UserInteraction
model_justification: Phone calls between leaders qualify as user interactions, though the examples are non-digital. schema.org's UserInteraction is the broadest fit among outdated candidates.
judge_notes: A phone call between heads of state typed as a web-page interaction.

schema_definition: Specifies the Person that is legally accountable for the CreativeWork.
example_usages: King [Organization] --accountablePerson--> Asha Sharma [Person]
model_justification: accountablePerson fits Organization → Person

schema_definition: An actor, e.g. in TV, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.
example_usages: Production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day [PublicationEvent] --actors--> Zendaya [Person]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Superseded plural form.

schema_definition: An organization that this person is affiliated with. For example, a school/university, a club, or a team.
example_usages: June Goh [Person] --affiliation--> Sparta [Organization]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/affiliation with as_is direction since Person → Organization aligns with the property's definition.
judge_notes: The subject is an economic-benefit node, not a person.

schema_definition: A person or organization attending the event.
example_usages: Israel [Country] --attendee--> US-Israel War on Iran [MilitaryConflict]
model_justification: Minted because no existing schema.org property fits the Country → MilitaryConflict signature as an as_is or inverse.
judge_notes: A country is put in the attendee slot of a clinical trial.

schema_definition: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.
example_usages: Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben [Person] --author--> AI Decodes Von Wandersleben's Letter [HistoricalTextDecryption]
model_justification: Schema.org's author property indicates the creator of a CreativeWork, which can include a HistoricalTextDecryption.
judge_notes: He authored the letter, not the decryption event.

schema_definition: Awards won by or for this item.
example_usages: Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam] --awards--> World Cup trophy [AwardTrophy]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Superseded plural form, and the range is Text.

schema_definition: The cause of a medical condition.
example_usages: Outbreak of Bundibugyo virus in DR Congo [Event] --cause--> Bundibugyo virus species [InfectiousAgentClass]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The outbreak-to-pathogen usage is apt despite the MedicalCondition domain.

schema_definition: The condition, complication, symptom, sign, etc. caused.
example_usages: Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv [Event] --causeOf--> Russia [Country]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "attack on Kyiv --causeOf--> Russia" reverses cause and agent.

schema_definition: A colleague of the person.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [Person] --colleagues--> Romain Montbabut [Person]
model_justification: The 'colleagues' property aligns with the Person → Person signature for professional peers.
judge_notes: Superseded plural form.

schema_definition: A competitor in a sports event.
example_usages: US Open [SportsEvent] --competitor--> Aryna Sabalenka [Person]
model_justification: Schema.org 'competitor' fits SportsEvent to Person for athlete participation in tournaments.

schema_definition: The basic containment relation between a place and one that contains it.
example_usages: artificial colorings [ChemicalSubstance] --containedIn--> ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: containedIn is Place to Place; used for a substance inside a food category.

schema_definition: The creator/author of this CreativeWork. This is the same as the Author property for CreativeWork.

model_justification: Reusing 'creator' in inverse direction to fit Product → Person.

schema_definition: The group the release is credited to if different than the byArtist. For example, Red and Blue is credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", but by Lady Gaga.

model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A MusicRelease credit property used for who issued a statement.

schema_definition: The date/time the message was received if a single recipient exists.

model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Pedro Sanchez --dateReceived--> Spain's World Cup champions".

schema_definition: The end date and time of the item (in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).
example_usages: Neymar [Person] --endDate--> Brazil [Country]
model_justification: Using endDate as the property for the retirement event, aligning with the subject (Person) and object (Country).

schema_definition: The most generic uni-directional social relation.
example_usages: Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam] --follows--> Fountain collapse in Ciudad Rodrigo [TragicIncident]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: schema.org follows is a social relation between people.

schema_definition: A person or organization who founded this organization.
example_usages: Common Space [Organization] --founder--> Bill Greer [Person]
model_justification: The founder property links an organization to its founder (Person/Organization), so we use it with inverse direction for Person → Organization.

schema_definition: The place where the Organization was founded.
example_usages: hackers [Organization] --foundingLocation--> China [Country]
model_justification: The 'foundingLocation' property fits the 'Organization → Country' signature for origin.

schema_definition: The Person's occupation. For past professions, use Role for expressing dates.
example_usages: Romain Montbabut [Person] --hasOccupation--> head baker [Occupation]
model_justification: The 'hasOccupation' property directly matches the Person → Occupation signature.

schema_definition: A common representation such as a protein sequence or chemical structure for this entity. For images use schema.org/image.
example_usages: Volodymyr Zelensky [Person] --hasRepresentation--> Zelensky’s plea for NATO air defense support [Statement]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A BioChemEntity property linking a person to his own statement.

schema_definition: Used to indicate a specific claim contained, implied, translated or refined from the content of a [[MediaObject]] or other [[CreativeWork]]. The interpreting party can be indicated using [[claimInterpreter]].
example_usages: Kevin Feige on Spider-Man's debut [Statement] --interpretedAsClaim--> Kevin Feige [Person]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The range is Claim; the object is the speaker.

schema_definition: A pointer to another product (or multiple products) for which this product is a consumable.

model_justification: The 'isConsumableFor' property fits the Product → FoodIngredient signature.
judge_notes: The salt is consumed for the bread, not the reverse.

schema_definition: Indicates a BioChemEntity that is (in some sense) a part of this BioChemEntity.
example_usages: saturated fats [ChemicalSubstance] --isPartOfBioChemEntity--> ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The part-hood is right; the BioChemEntity scoping is not.

schema_definition: Identifies the issue of publication; for example, "iii" or "2".

model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Asha Sharma --issueNumber--> her note on the restructuring".

schema_definition: The person or organization that countersigned the legislation. Depending on the legal context, a countersignature can indicate that the signed authority undertakes to assume responsibility for texts emanating from a person who is inviolable and irresponsible, (for example a King, Grand Duc or President), or that the authority is in charge of the implementation of the text.
example_usages: United States [Country] --legislationCountersignedBy--> Iran-US MoU on Strait of Hormuz [MemorandumOfUnderstanding]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/legislationCountersignedBy with as_is direction since Country → MemorandumOfUnderstanding aligns with Legislation → Organization/Person.
judge_notes: The memorandum is countersigned by the state, not the reverse.

schema_definition: An individual or organization that has some kind of responsibility for the legislation. Typically the ministry who is/was in charge of elaborating the legislation, or the adressee for potential questions about the legislation once it is published.
example_usages: 16 large wildfires active in Washington state [WildfireClusterEvent] --legislationResponsible--> National Weather Service [GovernmentOrganization]
model_justification: The wildfire cluster is warned by a government organization, aligning with 'legislationResponsible' for oversight.
judge_notes: "wildfires --legislationResponsible--> National Weather Service".

schema_definition: The manufacturer of the product.
example_usages: China [Country] --manufacturer--> renewable energy-related components [Product]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/manufacturer with as_is direction since Country → Product aligns with the property's domain/range.

schema_definition: A link to the ListItem that follows the current one.

model_justification: No schema.org property directly links HeatwaveForecastEvent to Event in this context; minting 'followedBy'.
judge_notes: Used to sequence two events; nextItem is scoped to ListItem.

schema_definition: Things owned by the organization or person.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [Person] --owns--> new venue in Paris [Restaurant]
model_justification: The 'owns' property directly matches the Person → Restaurant signature.

schema_definition: The 90th percentile value.
example_usages: ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory] --percentile90--> 71% [Number]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A distribution percentile used for a plain proportion.

schema_definition: Event that this person is a performer or participant in.
example_usages: Neymar [Person] --performerIn--> 2026 World Cup [SportsEvent]
model_justification: Using performerIn as the property for a person participating in a sports event.

schema_definition: An organization that acknowledges the validity, value or utility of a credential. Note: recognition may include a process of quality assurance or accreditation.
example_usages: Universal Pictures hits $4B mark [SaleEvent] --recognizedBy--> Universal Pictures [Corporation]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Credential-recognition property used for a box-office milestone.

schema_definition: The CreativeWork that captured all or part of this Event.

model_justification: The 'recordedIn' property links the InfrastructureDamageEvent to the UserBlocks CreativeWork that documented it, matching the reported relation.
judge_notes: NetBlocks recorded the blackout, not the reverse.

schema_definition: The URL at which a reply may be posted to the specified UserComment.
example_usages: Google [Organization] --replyToUrl--> Google retracts AI tool [ProductRetraction]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A comment-reply URL property linking a company to a retraction event.

schema_definition: The response (yes, no, maybe) to the RSVP.
example_usages: Google [Organization] --rsvpResponse--> AI tool could spread misinformation [MisinformationRisk]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Google --rsvpResponse--> AI tool could spread misinformation".

schema_definition: A pointer to products or services sought by the organization or person (demand).

model_justification: The emergency declaration seeks assistance from the president, matching the 'seeks' property for requests.
judge_notes: The range is Demand; the object is the person asked.

model_justification: Schema.org's sender property links a Message to its originator, aligning with the letter-sending context.

schema_definition: The spatialCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the place(s) which are the focus of the content. It is a subproperty of contentLocation intended primarily for more technical and detailed materials. For example with a Dataset, it indicates areas that the dataset describes: a dataset of New York weather would have spatialCoverage which was the place: the state of New York.
example_usages: Colombian earthquake [Event] --spatialCoverage--> Colombia [Country]
model_justification: spatialCoverage fits Event → City/Country with examples like 'New York State'.

schema_definition: A person or organization that supports a thing through a pledge, promise, or financial contribution. E.g. a sponsor of a Medical Study or a corporate sponsor of an event.
example_usages: Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo [Event] --sponsor--> World Health Organization [Organization]
model_justification: The 'sponsor' property from schema.org has a domain including Event and a range of Organization, which matches the instance 'Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo' (Event) --> 'World Health Organization' (Organization).

For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. E.g. John wrote a book from *January* to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.\n\nNote that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. example_usages: Rumored pre-party at Madison Square Garden [SocialEvent] --startTime--> 17:30 ET [DateTime]
model_justification: The schema.org 'startTime' property matches the 'SocialEvent → DateTime' signature for temporal markers.

schema_definition: A medical study or trial related to this entity.
example_usages: Toddler food processing analysis [ScientificStudy] --study--> peanut butter puffs [Product]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The object is what was studied, not a study.

schema_definition: An event that this event is a part of. For example, a collection of individual music performances might each have a music festival as their superEvent.

model_justification: Schema.org 'superEvent' (Event→Event) is used in inverse to map PrizeMoneyIncrease to its prior event.

schema_definition: Indicates a target EntryPoint, or url, for an Action.
example_usages: Russian attack on Kyiv on 2026-07-01 [Event] --target--> Kyiv [City]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: The total time required to perform instructions or a direction (including time to prepare the supplies), in [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).
example_usages: Toy Story 5 domestic performance [ScreeningEvent] --totalTime--> $1.06 billion [MonetaryAmount]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: Any FDA or other warnings about the drug (text or URL).

schema_definition: The size of the business in annual revenue.

model_justification: fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: Event type: Conference event.

model_justification: A NATO summit is a formal international conference, matching schema.org's ConferenceEvent definition with examples like summits and symposiums.

model_justification: Mentions describe a culinary award, fitting schema.org's FoodEvent as a gastronomic activity.

schema_definition: Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type.

model_justification: The example refers to a virus species, which fits as a subclass of InfectiousAgentClass.

schema_definition: A profession, may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification.

model_justification: Mentions are job roles (e.g., 'head baker'), aligning with schema.org's Occupation definition.

schema_definition: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.
